title: Native OpenVDB cache transfer: measured benefits and limits
scope: Accepted E3/E4 native C++ experiments on UInt16 Tree4 5/4/3. E1/E2 are superseded and excluded from conclusions.
question: Can the managed cache choices improve native OpenVDB, and what is suitable for upstream discussion?

summary.headline: The 64-leaf native cache with a short common path improved coherent throughput by 47.5% for reads and 32.8% for writes. Larger and colliding working sets regressed.

areas.name: Two implementation choices and layout counterfactual
areas.boundary: Leaf-cache storage, activity-word writes, and generated common-hit/miss layout.

areas.disposition: Seven bounded hypotheses including superseded preliminary attempts. Cache-plus-layout combinations supported locally; mask-only and layout-only comparisons were inconclusive. Full catalogue dispositions are in coverage.json.

hypotheses.claim: A 64-leaf secondary cache improves native coherent cached reads.
hypotheses.mechanism: Avoid repeated parent traversal when revisiting leaves.
hypotheses.prediction: All paired cache/stock read time ratios below one on coherent64.
hypotheses.falsification: Mixed paired directions or consistently higher time.
hypotheses.change: Add 64 direct-mapped leaf references with full origin checks and existing native invalidation callbacks.
hypotheses.result: read: stock 3.278530, cache 3.958364 ns/op; paired time ratio range 1.1519 to 1.2234.
hypotheses.maintainability: Experimental header overlay; generic library integration and additional platforms remain unvalidated.
hypotheses.codeComments: Patch comments state cache collision checks, invalidation and mask-word conditions.
hypotheses.decisionRationale: Preflight invalidation defect invalidates acceptance of this epoch; corrected tests and fresh measurements are recorded in E3.
risks: One Windows x64 compiler and processor.

hypotheses.claim: Skipping saturated activity-word updates improves native coherent cached writes.
hypotheses.mechanism: Avoid an idempotent activity-word read-modify-write when all 64 bits are already active.
hypotheses.prediction: All paired mask/stock write time ratios below one on coherent64.
hypotheses.falsification: Mixed paired directions or consistently higher time.
hypotheses.change: Guard only the native cached-buffer activity-bit update with a whole-word saturation test.
hypotheses.result: write: stock 4.876005, mask 4.686548 ns/op; paired time ratio range 0.9424 to 1.0963.
hypotheses.maintainability: Experimental header overlay; generic library integration and additional platforms remain unvalidated.
hypotheses.codeComments: Patch comments state cache collision checks, invalidation and mask-word conditions.
hypotheses.decisionRationale: Classifies the bounded transfer experiment. Guardrail workload results determine upstream suitability; no production patch is installed.
risks: One Windows x64 compiler and processor.
epochs: E1/E2 superseded; corrected native invalidation in E3/E4

hypotheses.claim: Separating secondary lookup from the common leaf-hit path makes the native cache improve coherent reads.
hypotheses.mechanism: E1 assembly showed a leaf-index lambda call in the cache variant's read loop. A small forced-inline entry point and non-inlined miss helper keep that call off last-leaf hits.
hypotheses.prediction: All paired split/stock read time ratios below one on coherent64; no unconditional leaf-lambda call on last-leaf hits in assembly.
hypotheses.falsification: Mixed paired directions, higher time, or an unconditional per-read helper call.
hypotheses.change: Preserve the original native membership predicate and tree fallback; move secondary lookup into an explicit miss helper.
hypotheses.result: read: stock 3.522404, split 2.367326 ns/op; paired time ratio range 0.5415 to 0.6749.
hypotheses.maintainability: Experimental header overlay; generic library integration and additional platforms remain unvalidated.
hypotheses.codeComments: Patch comments state cache collision checks, invalidation and mask-word conditions.
hypotheses.decisionRationale: Classifies the bounded transfer experiment. Guardrail workload results determine upstream suitability; no production patch is installed.
risks: One Windows x64 compiler and processor.
512 additional bytes per accessor; random512 and collision64 regress.

hypotheses.claim: Separating native common leaf hits from the miss helper improves coherent reads even without a larger cache.
hypotheses.mechanism: The native default traverses a template cache-level dispatcher. A small common-hit entry point may improve code layout independently of retaining additional leaves.
hypotheses.prediction: All paired split_only/stock read time ratios below one on coherent64, with the same 96-byte accessor and original parent caches.
hypotheses.falsification: Mixed paired directions or no improvement; larger/cache-collision/churn workloads identify regressions.
hypotheses.change: Use the explicit inline-hit and non-inline-miss layout with the stock single-leaf/parent caches and no secondary slots or activity guard.

retainedChanges: Native reproduction harness, guarded header prototype, focused assembly and measurement evidence.
Existing upstream OpenVDB checkout and the managed library remain unchanged.
decisions: The evidence supports proposing a configurable secondary leaf cache with a short common path. The 64-slot option adds 512 bytes per accessor.
The saturated-word guard was inconclusive in isolated native coherent-write comparisons. Its adoption needs further evidence.
The layout-only change did not reproduce the coherent gain. No unconditional replacement of the current native default is justified by these workloads.
correctness: Each executable tests signed cache collisions, copying, assignment across trees, explicitly invalidated direct tile replacement, clearing, explicit cache erasure, mask reactivation and tree destruction.
Every timed sample validates all voxel values/activity through tree lookups independent of the accessor; read checksums are consumed and verified.
All variants have identical coordinate hashes, topology and active voxel counts for every workload.
Accepted churn checks every voxel in the resulting leaf after each sample and includes node detachment, deletion, cache invalidation and rematerialization in timing.
E4 accessor sizes: stock and layout-only 96 bytes; 64-leaf cache 608 bytes. E3/E4 measured all variants after correcting the invalidation preflight.

generatedCode.summary: The accepted cached native read/write loops inline leaf-hit checks and buffer access. Calls to getValueSecondary/setValueSecondary occur on miss paths. Focused annotated listings are retained.

validityThreats: Only AMD Ryzen 9 5950X, Windows x64 and MSVC Release. No cross-machine claim.
The 64-leaf fixture exactly fits the secondary cache; random512 and collision64 deliberately test losing distributions.
The mask experiment modifies the native cached-buffer write path; it is not a general NodeMask API change.
The cache overlay changes accessor object size and layout. It is a prototype, not an ABI-compatible upstream patch.
Focused tests do not establish all OpenVDB types, APIs, threading configurations or full upstream-suite compatibility.
The shared performance lock is cooperative; external CPU snapshots are retained in raw/environment.json.
E1/E2 preflight omitted required invalidation before direct Tree.addTile. Those results are retained as superseded and excluded; E3/E4 rebuilt and reran all accepted measurements.
Direct Tree.addTile requires explicit invalidation. The accepted churn workload uses Tree.stealNode, whose implementation clears registered accessors before detaching the node.
The layout-only control measures the call-layout choice without extra cache storage or the mask guard. It is distinct from the 608-byte cached variants.

Power/CPU load snapshots do not prove continuous isolation. E4 snapshots showed CPU 8 at 31% before and 9% after; total load 15% before and 0% after. All samples, including slower launches, remain included.

Absolute timings from this native vector-coordinate harness should not be used for an exact ratio against the earlier managed fixed-array harness. All stated improvement ratios are contemporaneous native-versus-native comparisons.
